Chapter 8: Developing Leadership Habits—Inspiring Action and Setting the Example
You know, leadership isn’t just for folks with official titles or fancy business cards. It’s really a set of habits and attitudes that anyone can develop, no matter where they find themselves. At its heart, leadership is about helping others believe in themselves, sparking action, and rallying people around common goals.
One of the most powerful ways to lead? It’s by setting the example. People naturally gravitate toward those who walk the talk—those who actually live out the values they talk about. So, what does that look like? It means showing integrity in every decision, staying optimistic even when things get tough, and being open to learning from your own mistakes.
There are a few key habits that really drive big thinking as a leader:
First, set clear and ambitious goals—and talk about them with real energy. When you’re excited, it’s contagious.
Next, show persistence and adaptability. When you hit a roadblock, don’t just throw in the towel. Instead, figure out a new way forward and let others see that process.
Delegation is huge, too. Trust your team to use their strengths, and let them take charge of their part.
And don’t forget feedback—offer it regularly, and make time to celebrate what you’ve accomplished together.
Just picture a project leader who doesn’t just brag about the wins, but also shares the bumps along the way. Someone who invites everyone’s ideas and keeps the focus on the big picture. That’s the kind of leadership that makes people feel like they truly belong and inspires them to reach for more.
Creating this kind of environment—where it’s safe to try new things, ask questions, and even challenge old ways of thinking—is essential if you want real innovation and long-term growth.
There’s another piece to this puzzle: recognizing and nurturing potential in others. Whether you’re mentoring, coaching, or just cheering someone on, you’re helping people discover what they’re capable of—and that can be life-changing.
Here’s the thing—these leadership habits aren’t built overnight. It’s about the daily choices you make and how you treat people, day in and day out. Over time, these habits become part of who you are, shaping not just your own results, but the entire culture around you—at work, in your community, wherever you lead.
And that’s what sets the stage for our final big idea: how to keep that spark of big thinking alive through constant growth and renewal.
